context: Identical cards numbered from 1 to N, mixed well, one card drawn at random.
stem: A set of identical cards numbered from 1 to {=N} with no repetition is mixed up well, and a card is drawn randomly. Let A be the event that the drawn card has a number divisible by {=m}, and B the event that the drawn card has a number divisible by {=k}. Use a Venn diagram to calculate the probability that A or B occurs (the card is in A or in B or in both). Write the answer as a fraction in its simplest form.
solution: Numbers divisible by both {=m} and {=k} are the multiples of {=L}, so $n(A\cap B)={=nAB}$.
In the Venn diagram the common part is counted once: $n(A\cup B)={=nA}+{=nB}-{=nAB}={=u}$.
$P(A\cup B)=\frac{n(A\cup B)}{n(S)}=\frac{{=u}}{{=N}}$, which in simplest form is the answer.
